ROOT CAUSE for a large share of the missing-website backlog: the BiblioCommons fetcher discards each event id at fetch time, so no event URL can be reconstructed afterwards. ROOT CAUSE FOUND for a defect that has been producing false warnings for days. deals_overlay.py writes a deal_source provenance key on every row it stamps, but deal_source is not one of the 19 schema-v3.1 BASE fields, and build_guide.py line 22 rebuilds each row as {k: it.get(k,'') for k in BASE}. The field is therefore created by the overlay, consumed in the same run, and DESTROYED at build -- it never reaches the published CSV, so the next run's carried base arrives with it blank. Two silent failures followed. (a) The overlay's `owned` carve-out, which exists so that edits to standing_deals.csv actually take effect on a re-run, tests deal_source and so was False for every carried row: the overlay was a NO-OP on exactly the rows it was written to refresh, meaning a corrected deal_description would never have reached the live app for any venue stamped on a previous run. (b) deals_yield.py attributes by deal_source, so sources whose venues were all stamped earlier reported 0 and warned forever. Fixed with deal_provenance_restore.py, a pre-pass that reconstructs the attribution by exact whitespace-normalised full-string equality against standing_deals.csv -- NOT the substring keyword scan CLAUDE.md forbids -- and refuses to guess when a description is claimed by two sources.

item: geo0826.py hardcodes its own input path
description: geo0826.py crashed under bycat_shim.py with TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not str. The shape mismatch is the known one -- the helper wants {category: [rows]} and _compiled_work.json is a flat list -- but there is a SECOND defect the shim cannot handle: geo0826.py line 74 reads os.path.join(HERE, '_compiled_work.json') directly and IGNORES argv, so bycat_shim's reshaped temp file never reaches it and the helper re-reads the flat original. Wrote geo_shim.py, which reshapes the file the helper actually reads, runs it VERBATIM as a subprocess, and flattens back using injected index keys so row order is restored exactly. Running the helper unmodified matters more than the convenience of editing it -- a local edit is how the curated_tag vocabulary drift reached 83 live rows.
resolution_note: geo_shim.py added; row count and order asserted identical across the round trip. The real fix is for geo0826.py to honour argv - bycat_shim is correct as written.

MiniSota Play Cafe (Maple Grove) was present in 2 rows (events + restaurants) despite SKILL.md 404 declaring it permanently closed 2026-04-29 with an explicit 'do NOT re-add'. Both rows dropped. ROOT CAUSE: no pass in the pipeline reads SKILL.md's closed-venue declarations, and closure_filter.py cannot help -- it reads a row's own title for a cancellation notice, and 'MiniSota Play Cafe' announces nothing. The row simply rode the carried base forward. A standing closed-venue denylist derived from SKILL.md is the fix.

SAME ADDRESS / DIFFERENT TITLE is a structural blind spot in the whole dedup chain: every pass blocks on an exact normalized TITLE and then compares place, and dupsweep.py requires title AND address AND date to match. So one venue written up N ways by N sources never collides. Sovereign Grounds -- ONE coffeehouse per SKILL.md 407 -- was carrying 7 rows. 7 hand-adjudicated groups collapsed 16 rows to 7 via step8_venue_repair.py: sovereign_grounds 7->1, brasa_grand_ave 3->1, littles_and_lattes 2->1, angel_food_bakery 2->1, red_cow_50th 2->1, red_cow_selby 2->1, st_paul_tap 2->1.

The same-address collapse is a HAND TABLE, not a rule, because the automatic version is wrong: scanning restaurants+parks for 'same normalized address, differing titles sharing a distinctive token' returned 7 groups of which 2 are false positives a rule would have merged -- Chipotle Mankato / Noodles & Company Mankato (two chains sharing one mall address at 1600 Warren St) and Lake Phalen Beach / Phalen Regional Park (a beach inside a park). Recorded in step8_venue_repair.KEEP_APART so a later reader does not 'fix' them.

Red Cow is the case that proves the precision rule: 9 rows, genuine multi-location chain. Merging on the name would be the chain-collapse error CLAUDE.md forbids. Only 2 pairs merged, each on evidence that is NOT the name -- 3624 W 50th St appearing verbatim on two rows, and two rows both resolving to the venue's own per-location URL redcowmn.com/st-paul-selby-avenue/ (Selby Ave is in Cathedral Hill). Uptown, North Loop, Wayzata and Rochester correctly remain 4 separate rows.

dupsweep.py na() gap: it maps 'ste'->'st' but leaves 'suite' untouched, so '15670 Edgewood Dr Ste 120' and '15670 Edgewood Dr, Suite 120' normalize DIFFERENTLY and the two Littles and Lattes rows could never collide on address. Suite/unit designators should be stripped entirely rather than half-abbreviated. Not changed this run -- it is a safety helper with a 30-case suite and the change belongs with a test, not a post-publish hotfix. Carried for the next run.

Merge survivor is chosen by field COMPLETENESS, not by address correctness, so the richest row can be the one carrying the wrong address -- and its lat/lon was geocoded FROM that wrong address. Sovereign Grounds had exactly such a row (2400 Third Avenue South, sourced from a minnesotaparent.com listicle sitting in the `website` field). step8_venue_repair.py therefore blanks lat/lon whenever the survivor's own address differs from the canonical one, because STEP 4.9 SKIPS populated coordinates and the mismatch would never self-correct on any later run. All 7 survivors verified in-bbox and within ~2 km of their street address after re-geocode.

TRIPWIRE CALIBRATION: the play-cafe count read 19 BEFORE this repair and 13 after, against a documented floor of ~12. It passes either way, but 6 of the original 19 were duplicate Sovereign Grounds rows and 1 was the closed MiniSota -- i.e. the margin above the floor was largely fragmentation and a closed venue, not coverage. A count-only tripwire cannot see this; reading the 19 TITLES is what surfaced both defects. Recommend the check also report DISTINCT venue titles, and note the true margin is now 1 row above the floor.

SELF-CAUGHT VERIFICATION DEFECT: my first attempt at a pre-change control ran `build_guide.py >/dev/null 2>&1 && end_date_pass.py`. build_guide.py takes its source as argv[1] and defaults to '_compiled_base.json', which does not exist -- so it raised FileNotFoundError, the && short-circuited, and NEITHER script ran. The artifacts were unchanged, so the hash comparison reported SAME and the control looked like it passed while proving nothing. Re-run correctly as `build_guide.py .pre_step8_compiled.json` with stderr visible, it genuinely reproduced all 6 published blobs. LESSON: a control that compares outputs must assert the producing command's exit status, and suppressing stderr in a verification step converts a crash into a false PASS.

LATENT DEFECT IN THIS TASK'S OWN PUBLISH GUARD, found while publishing today and fixed in-run. The 2026-09-16 concurrent-dispatch finding requires error_log.csv to be published with optimistic concurrency, and requires a 409 to be repaired by RE-APPLYING our own rows onto the new base, identifying them by exact full-row equality. That guard read the remote base from the contents API's `content` field. error_log.csv is now 1,299,503 bytes, and GitHub's contents API returns `content` as an EMPTY STRING above 1 MB while still returning correct metadata and HTTP 200. So the base decoded to zero bytes, and the guard computed 4,041 rows as 'mine' when the true answer was 9. No 409 occurred today, so no damage was done -- but had one occurred, the repair would have appended the ENTIRE file onto the new base and roughly doubled the log. The guard written to prevent a lost update would instead have caused mass duplication, which is the worse of the two failures. The same bug also produced a false verification FAIL on a publish that had in fact landed correctly on the first attempt, causing two further no-op PUTs (GitHub correctly treated them as idempotent and created exactly one commit, 80c856015e). Fixed two ways: identity is now checked against the contents API's `sha` field, which IS the git blob SHA-1 and is returned at any size, and bytes are fetched from the git BLOBS API with the raw media type, whose result is asserted to hash back to that sha. A sanity gate now also refuses any re-apply claiming more than 10% of the file as 'own rows'. The generalisation is this project's own rule reaching the transport layer: a 200 with a structurally empty body passes every status check, exactly like the parked-domain source logged 2026-09-16 -- and a guard that has never been made to FAIL on purpose is an assertion you merely hope is wired up. This one had never fired, because the log only crossed 1 MB recently.
